definitions.explanation: A ballot cast with nothing written on it, used to record turnout without choosing any candidate or option.

definitions.gloss: white ballot; vote in favor (in the Diet)
definitions.explanation: In Japan's Diet, a white voting slip indicating approval of a motion, as opposed to a blue slip for opposition.

examples.japanese: {白票|はくひょう}を{投|とう}じた。
{白票|はくひょう}も{投票|とうひょう}{率|りつ}に{含|ふく}まれる。
examples.english: Blank ballots are also counted in the voter turnout.

examples.japanese: {支持|しじ}できる{候補|こうほ}がいなかったので、{抗議|こうぎ}の{意味|いみ}で{白票|はくひょう}を{投|とう}じた。
examples.english: There was no candidate I could support, so I cast a blank ballot as a form of protest.

examples.japanese: {議員|ぎいん}は{白票|はくひょう}を{投|とう}じて{賛成|さんせい}した。
examples.english: The lawmaker cast a white ballot to vote in favor.

examples.japanese: {採決|さいけつ}では{白票|はくひょう}が{過半数|かはんすう}を{占|し}めた。
examples.english: In the vote, white ballots made up the majority.

examples.japanese: {参議院|さんぎいん}の{採決|さいけつ}では、{賛成|さんせい}を{表|あらわ}す{白票|はくひょう}と{反対|はんたい}を{表|あらわ}す{青票|あおひょう}が{使|つか}われる。
examples.english: In House of Councillors votes, white ballots indicating approval and blue ballots indicating opposition are used.

notes:
Compound of {白|はく} (white) + {票|ひょう} (ballot, vote). The word has two distinct uses depending on context.

USAGE:
- In ordinary elections, a {白票|はくひょう} is a blank ballot — a deliberate abstention that still counts toward turnout.
- In the Diet's standing-vote procedure, a white slip means approval and a blue slip ({青票|あおひょう}) means opposition.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {白票|はくひょう}を{投|とう}じる: to cast a blank (or white) ballot
- {白票|はくひょう}が{過半数|かはんすう}を{占|し}める: white ballots form a majority

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {青票|あおひょう}: blue ballot — the opposing vote in Diet procedure
- {棄権|きけん}: abstention — declining to vote at all, not casting a blank ballot
